report.tagline: OYO turns small, independent budget hotels into a branded chain you can book in an app.
report.simpleSummary: OYO does not own most of its hotels. It signs up small hotel owners, puts its brand on them, lists them in its app and helps fill rooms. You book a cheap, clean-enough room in almost any Indian town for a few hundred to a couple of thousand rupees. OYO takes a cut of what the hotel earns. It also owns Motel 6 in the US and holiday homes in Europe.

overview.whatItDoes: OYO is a platform for budget hotels. Small hotel owners join OYO, get its brand, software and bookings, and pay OYO a share of revenue. Travellers book rooms in the OYO app or on travel sites like MakeMyTrip. Outside India it runs Motel 6 and Studio 6 in the US and vacation homes in Europe under brands like Belvilla and DanCenter.
howItWorks: OYO signs a hotel owner, checks the property and brands it, for example as OYO, Townhouse, Collection O or Capital O.
The hotel gets OYO's software to manage rooms, prices and check-ins.
OYO sets prices that move with demand and lists rooms on its own app and on other booking sites.
A guest books, often with discounts or OYO Wizard membership offers, and pays online or at the hotel.
OYO keeps a commission and passes the rest to the owner.
Premium brands like Palette, Townhouse Oak and the Sunday hotels target higher-paying guests.
overview.valueProposition: For guests: a predictable, cheap room you can book in seconds in almost any town. For owners: more bookings and better tech without spending on marketing.

painPoints.howSolved: OYO brand with basic standards, photos and reviews.

painPoints.pain: Hard to find and book small-town hotels online.

businessModel.summary: OYO is asset-light: it does not own most hotels. It earns mostly a commission from hotels and homes on its platform, plus income from Motel 6 franchise fees in the US and vacation home rentals in Europe. It now makes a profit after years of losses.

revenueStreams.detail: A share of each room night booked through OYO.
Belvilla, DanCenter and others rent holiday homes and take a cut.
Bought in 2024 for about $525 million; earns franchise fees from motel owners.
Fees for software and add-on services.

businessModel.pricing: Room prices vary by city and date. Many OYO rooms in India list between about ₹600 and ₹2,500 a night. Premium brands cost more.
costDrivers: Commissions paid to other booking sites
Sales and quality teams that sign and audit hotels
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a ₹1,200 room night in India. If OYO keeps a 20% to 25% commission, it earns about ₹240 to ₹300. If the booking came through a travel site, OYO pays maybe ₹100 to ₹150 of that away. Discounts and support take more. That is why OYO pushes direct bookings in its own app and loyalty plans. Earlier, OYO guaranteed owners fixed income, which caused huge losses when rooms stayed empty. Moving to pure commission made each booking profitable.

howTheyGetUsers: Huge supply in small towns where few other brands exist
Listing on MakeMyTrip, Goibibo, Booking.com and Google
Discounts and coupons for first bookings
whatBringsUsersBack: Saved details and fast rebooking in the app
growth.moat: OYO has more budget hotels signed up across small Indian towns than anyone else. A rival would need years of door-to-door sales to match that supply, and the data on pricing in each town.

competitors.name: Treebo and FabHotels
competitors.positioning: Branded budget hotel chains with tighter quality.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: OYO has far more hotels and towns but quality is more uneven.

competitors.name: MakeMyTrip and Goibibo
competitors.positioning: Online travel agents listing all hotels.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: OYO brands and manages its hotels; MakeMyTrip only lists. MakeMyTrip is also a sales channel for OYO.

competitors.name: Airbnb
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: OYO is mainly cheap hotels; Airbnb is homes and longer stays.

competitors.name: Booking.com and Agoda
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Stronger in big cities and abroad; OYO wins in small Indian towns.

improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Check-in denial rate and repeat rate

Guest-uploaded recent photos with date stamps
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Rating gap between expected and actual

improvementIdeas.idea: Payout on a fixed day with a public tracker for owners

pmLessons: Fast growth on paper can hide a broken model. OYO's old minimum-guarantee deals grew supply but lost money on empty rooms.
In a marketplace, both sides must trust you. Ignoring owners hurt OYO's supply and brand.
Pivots are normal. OYO went from listings to managed hotels to franchise and back to light commission, and profit came after.
A brand only means something if quality is consistent.

interviewQuestions.question: OYO's rating in tier-3 towns is falling. How would you fix it?
interviewQuestions.hint: Break down by hotel, complaint type and booking source. Fix top offenders, add audits, delist repeat bad hotels.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase direct bookings in the OYO app?
interviewQuestions.hint: Price advantage, loyalty, better search, offline-to-app nudges at check-in.

interviewQuestions.question: What should OYO's north star metric be?
interviewQuestions.hint: Good stays, not just bookings. Show the KPI tree with supply, demand and quality.

interviewQuestions.question: Was the Motel 6 acquisition a good idea?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at fit, profit, debt and whether OYO's tech improves motel occupancy.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you design the owner app to reduce owner churn?
interviewQuestions.hint: Clear earnings, payout timeline, simple dispute flow, demand forecasts.
